summary.headline: Apollo Tyres Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose over 16% YoY to INR 79.7bn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.7% on a ~25% raw-material spike.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew over 16% YoY to INR 79.7bn with EBITDA of INR 8.6bn (10.7% margin), the strongest YoY revenue growth in 16 quarters per management. India revenue rose ~26% to INR 59.2bn but India EBITDA margin fell to 11.1% from 15.3%, as raw-material costs rose ~25% since April 2026. Europe revenue fell 12% YoY to EUR 157m on truck/agri weakness linked to the Enschede plant closure, with EBITDA margin at 10.3%. Management pushed through 13-15% cumulative price increases to date and guided to mid-to-high single-digit RM cost push from Q2 to Q3.

segments.name: India Replacement
segments.commentary: PCR grew about mid-teens volume and Truck high single digits; two-wheeler volume rose ~25-26%, with overall Replacement volume in low double digits. Price increases of up to 15% were implemented.

segments.name: India OEM
segments.commentary: OEM was the fastest-growing channel with ~25%+ volume growth in Q2; OEM price increases are largely formula-linked with a one-quarter lag, with some negotiated increases.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export volumes were broadly flat YoY in Q2; PCR exports were weak and management is being conservative on export outlook.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue down 12% YoY to EUR 157m on truck and agri weakness tied to Enschede closure; PCR (and PCLT, Vredestein) gained share, with Apollo-branded PCLT volume up over 50%. Reifen revenue flattish, Q2 margins seasonally subdued.

guidance_outlook: Raw-material basket expected to rise mid-to-high single digits from Q2 to Q3 FY27; management now expects RM to peak toward end of CY/FY, stabilising from next year (caveated).
Management said the 13-15% cumulative price increases (to end-October) would see full impact in Q3; planned increases in Dec/Jan depend on RM and competition.
India volume growth expected at mid-to-high single digits YoY in Q3 as the base is elevated by last year's GST change and BCCI; revenue growth to come mainly from pricing.
Europe expected to meet budgets from Q3 FY27; operations largely stable by next financial year; medium-term target of high-teen operating margins in Europe.
Enschede dismantling and closure to take two to three more quarters; Enschede-related cleanup costs expected to continue in trickles, not significant.
Net debt to EBITDA expected to stay within target range despite expansion; ROCE may dip short term but mid-teens ROCE targeted at steady state.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 consolidated net capex around INR 15bn, broadly in line with full-year plan.
Plant capacity utilisation around 85-90% across plants, cited as reason to keep expanding capex to avoid losing market share.
TBR manufacturing relocated from Hungary to AP (India) plant; Hungary is the sole operating plant in Europe for high-end tyres, with smaller sizes supplied from India.
Enschede plant operations stopped end of Q1 FY27; dismantling and sale of equipment to take two to three quarters.
Management referenced announced expansion plans; additional debt expected as expansion proceeds (no amounts quantified on call).
demand_pricing: Raw-material basket up ~25% YoY in Q2 FY27; natural rubber up ~25-26% YoY and above INR 300/kg in India; crude-linked derivatives up 28-35%; steel cord up low double digits.
Cumulative replacement price increases of 13-15% across categories by end-October (management said 11-13% realised on average earlier in the call); TBR price increases 13-14%.
Industry-wide price increases broadly in line with peers; Apollo leading in some categories and following in others.
Management said RM cost push of ~25% in H1 would have required 16-17% price increases to fully hold margins; the gap is being closed gradually.
Exports exposed to volatility across Europe, America and Middle East/SE Asia; no recovery timeline given.
Management pointed to strong domestic demand momentum and sustained OEM price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Volume split across OEM, Replacement and exports, and category performance?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM volume grew ~25%+, Replacement low double digits, exports flattish. Within Replacement, two-wheeler grew ~25-26%, PCR mid-teens and truck high single digits in India.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase is needed and planned to protect gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 16-17% needed to hold margins against ~25% RM inflation; 11-13% achieved on average so far, 13-15% taken by end-October, with further 1-2% increases announced in October and more planned for Dec/Jan.

qa_highlights.question: Is Europe weakness company-specific or market-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: market slowdown plus supply disruption from the Enschede to Hungary/India transition. Management expects Q3 to meet budget; PCLT grew 5% and Apollo PCLT volume rose over 50%, while agri and TBR declined.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital outlook for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 included plant-shutdown payouts that are now behind; H2 expected to show more stable working capital and seasonally better cash flows in Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the strong control on other expenses and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Weekly/fortnightly leadership review, A&P discipline and travel cost controls; freight not controllable. Q4 other expenses hard to call, with management ready to tighten further if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Price pass-through in Q3 and OEM pricing mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Full impact of the 13-15% increases expected in Q3; further action depends on RM in Nov/Dec. OEM pricing is largely formula-linked with a one-quarter lag, some OEM increases negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term ROCE and capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term ROCE dip expected during capex cycle; mid-teens ROCE targeted at steady state. Capex is needed to hold 85-90% utilisation; more debt likely as expansion proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin trajectory and RM peak (Basudeb Banerjee)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects RM to peak toward end of the year and stabilise from next year, subject to volatility. Himanshu Sharma said historical margin troughs were single digit, versus ~11% now.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure in Q3-Q4 if price pass-through lags RM inflation; analyst estimate of 300-400bps further margin risk was not rebutted.
Volatility in natural rubber and crude; management said RM is not expected to stabilise before next year.
Europe execution: Enschede closure, supply chain reorganisation, SAP S/4HANA rollout in Europe, and agri/TBR volume loss.
Export demand recovery uncertain; management being conservative.
Other expenses in Q4 could rise seasonally; management did not commit to maintaining Q2 cost discipline.
Rising debt to fund expansion; net debt to EBITDA below 1x but expected to rise; granular interest details deferred to IR team.
CFO transition: new CFO Ravi Kumar Shingari; Chairman Neeraj did not join the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and pricing discipline in India and on balance-sheet strength, but cautious and hedged on raw-material peak timing, Europe recovery and exports. Several specific questions (interest-cost detail, price-pass-through quantum, working capital) were deferred to the IR team offline.
key_quotes: While raw material prices will eventually stabilize and may even soften over a period of time, our objective is to ensure that the enhanced pricing discipline demonstrated during this cycle becomes a permanent feature of the business.
As on 30th September 2026, consolidated net debt to EBITDA stood at just 0.9 times, providing substantial capacity to fund future growth while maintaining a prudent capital structure.
Quarter three onwards we are expected to meet our budgets and probably get the revenue in line and the volumes in line.
Over the medium term, we remain committed to building a European business capable of delivering high teen operating margins.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 85-90% with management saying capex is needed to avoid losing share, H1 net capex ~INR 15bn, and more debt expected as expansion proceeds; amounts not yet quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided Q3 India volume only mid-to-high single digits and is conservative on exports; RM inflation and gap to full price pass-through cap upside to guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: RM basket to rise mid-to-high single digits Q2 to Q3, price pass-through lags (13-15% taken vs 16-17% needed), Q4 other expenses could rise seasonally, and Europe recovery is pending from Q3 with the high-teens margin target already slipped.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed on the call.

rows.label: Further price increases in Dec/Jan
rows.why: 1-2% further increases announced in October with more planned for Dec/Jan; full impact of 13-15% taken so far comes in Q3, against 16-17% needed to fully hold margins.

rows.label: Europe back to budget and normalised margins
rows.why: Management expects Europe to meet budgets from Q3 FY27 and stable operations with normalised margins from FY28, but the high-teen margin target has slipped and Enschede dismantling takes 2-3 more quarters.

rows.label: Stable H2 working capital
rows.why: H1 plant-shutdown payouts are behind and H2 is expected to show more stable working capital and seasonally better Europe cash flow; no amounts given.
